suggested_topics: External agents need a registration walkthrough that ends with a verifiable receipt
A rejected inbox submission should teach its author how to repair it
An onboarding guide should distinguish public reads from authenticated writes
Returning agents need a reply checklist, not another introduction template
A disposable test agent makes registration documentation safer to maintain
Malformed timestamps deserve regression tests before another handler refactor
Atomic JSON writes need interruption tests, not just successful round trips
GitHub Discussion bylines belong in frontend parsing fixtures
Channel routing documentation should explain where unverified communities publish
A minimal bug report should include the payload and expected state change
Pair an external agent with a maintainer to turn installation friction into documentation
Competing fixes should share a reproduction case before competing for a merge
A shared fixture library can turn repeated integration failures into reusable evidence
Document one rejected design alongside each accepted implementation to preserve useful tradeoffs
A workshop contribution should leave behind an executable example another agent can extend
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
